newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities ended higher.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities ended higher.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended slightly higher across the board in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Monday.
"It has been quiet in the market today for bonds and treasury bills with the upcoming Christmas holidays," a local dealer said.
"Treasury bill yields and the interbank rate eased slightly today and bond prices ended higher but it has no impact on the market. Volume was moderate," he added
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.90/1.85 percent compared with last Friday's yield of 2.05/2.00 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.20/2.15 percent against 2.30/2.25 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.00/98.05 from Friday's close of S$97.98/98.03, September 2001 at S$97.00/97.05 versus S$96.86/96.91 and June 2003 at S$95.00/95.05 against S$94.86/94.91.
The overnight interbank offered rate eased to 2-5/8 2-1/4 percent from Friday's 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent.
